summary:
Lunar Navigator is an interactive web application created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to simplify the exploration and comparison of potential Moon landing sites. Missions to the lunar south pole face extreme lighting conditions, limited sunlight, and communication challenges with Earth. Understanding how these factors change with location and time is important for planning safe and effective missions.

Our website provides an interactive 3D Moon where users can rotate, explore, and select potential landing sites. The site analysis feature provides information about the Sun's position, sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and communication conditions for a selected location and date. Users can also compare two landing sites side by side to quickly identify their differences and understand the trade-offs between possible locations.

          Lunar Navigator combines scientific concepts with an intuitive and visually engaging interface, making complex lunar information easier to understand. It is designed not only for mission-planning exploration but also for students, educators, researchers, space enthusiasts, and the general public. The website also provides links to useful NASA and space-science resources for deeper investigation. By turning complex information into interactive visual experiences, Lunar Navigator helps users better understand the challenges of exploring and establishing missions near the Moon's south pole.
details:
Lunar Navigator is an interactive web application designed to help users explore, analyze, and compare potential landing sites near the Moon’s south pole. The project addresses the challenge of understanding extreme lighting conditions and communication constraints that can affect lunar missions.

  • The application provides an interactive 3D Moon where users can rotate the Moon and select landing-site markers. After selecting a site, users can view important information such as its location, Sun elevation, sunlight conditions, Earth visibility, and communication opportunities. The comparison feature allows users to examine two landing sites side by side and understand the advantages and trade-offs of each location. A resources section also provides links to useful NASA and space-science tools for further research.
  • The main benefit of Lunar Navigator is that it transforms complex scientific information into an intuitive and visual experience. Instead of requiring users to understand complicated scientific interfaces, the website presents important information in a simple and accessible format. Its intended impact is to support mission-planning exploration while also helping students, educators, researchers, space enthusiasts, and the general public better understand the challenges of lunar landing exploration.
  • The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with web-based 3D visualization technologies used to create the interactive Moon experience. The application is designed to run directly in a web browser without requiring specialized hardware.
  • Creativity was a major part of the project. We combined a visually engaging space-themed interface, interactive 3D visualization, site analysis, and side-by-side comparison into one platform. Our team considered usability, accessibility, visual clarity, scientific relevance, performance, and the need to communicate complex information in a simple way. We also considered the limitations of approximate browser-based calculations and clearly indicate that mission-grade analysis should be verified using authoritative NASA tools.

Overall, Lunar Navigator aims to make lunar landing-site exploration more understandable, interactive, and engaging while encouraging people to learn more about the science and engineering behind future Moon missions.
